max_tire.note: Same axles and front suspension as the wagon, where INEOS Forum owners run 285/75R17 on stock suspension and 285/70R17 without rubbing. The spare lives in the bed, so there's no rear-door carrier to fight.

DVA Mechanics says 35s need at least 2 in of lift; a Quartermaster owner recommends narrow 35s (255/85R17, 35x10.5) on near-factory-offset wheels. Ineos Australia's Kaiju build ran 315/70R17 with JMACX remote-reservoir shocks.

identify.intro: Quartermasters come as Fieldmaster, Trialmaster, Black and Trialmaster X in the US, and spec matters more than year for off-road use.

items.head: Lockers
items.body: The centre diff lock is standard. Front and rear lockers come on the Trialmaster or with the Rough Pack; the switches are in the overhead panel and the centre lock is on the transfer lever.

items.head: Steering generation
items.body: MY2026 trucks have the variable-ratio box and roughly 5% tighter turning circle; earlier trucks have the slow recirculating-ball setup unless an aftermarket pump kit has been fitted.

items.head: Body type
items.body: US trucks are all double-cab wellside pickups. The cab-chassis for trays is an Australia/New Zealand model.

items.head: Bed equipment
items.body: Some trucks were built without bed rails and some dealers fit L-track; look for neat, sealed holes. Check where the spare lives, since it stands in the bed from the factory.

items.head: Engine
items.body: US trucks are BMW B58 3.0 petrol; the B57 diesel was sold in Europe, Australia and New Zealand.

capability.note: US launch figure; 907 kg petrol / 832 kg diesel in Australia
